title: What RAG is, with no jargon
summary: AI chatbots have never read your documents, and when they do not know something they often make up a confident answer. RAG fixes that by looking up the right paragraph first and handing it to the AI along with the question.
html:
You have probably used ChatGPT or something like it. You type a question, it writes an answer. It is good at this because it learned from an enormous amount of text from the internet.

At work it has two problems.

It has never read your documents. Your company's HR policy, your team's runbooks, last month's support tickets. None of that was in what it learned from. Ask it how many days of leave you get, and it simply does not know.

It rarely says "I don't know". More often it writes something that sounds right. Ask about your leave policy and it might say "most companies offer around 20 days" in a perfectly confident tone. A confident answer that is not true has a name: a hallucination.

The fix is the obvious one

Before you ask the AI, look the answer up yourself and paste it in.

Say your HR handbook contains this sentence: "Full time employees receive 24 days of paid leave per year." You send the AI this:

Here is a paragraph from our HR handbook:
"Full time employees receive 24 days of paid leave per year."

Question: How many days of leave do I get?

Now it answers "24 days", and it can say where that came from. It is not guessing any more. It is reading. Everything inside that box, the pasted paragraph plus the question, is called the prompt: the full message you send to the AI.

That is RAG. The whole idea. Everything else in this course is about doing that one thing well and automatically, when there are ten thousand documents instead of one sentence.

What the three letters mean

R is for Retrieval. Retrieval just means looking something up. In the example, that was you, searching the handbook for the right sentence.

A is for Augmented. Augmented just means added to. You added what you found to the question.

G is for Generation. Generation just means writing. The AI writes the answer. People call this kind of AI an LLM, short for large language model. ChatGPT is an LLM. So is Claude.

The analogy that fits best is a closed book exam versus an open book exam. In a closed book exam you answer from memory, and if you cannot remember, you might bluff. In an open book exam you look it up first. RAG turns the AI's exam into an open book one.

Why not paste in the whole handbook?

Fair question, and it has three answers. The AI can only read so much at once, and a company's documents are far more than that. Sending more text costs more money and takes longer. And when you hand it a huge pile, it gets worse at noticing the one sentence that matters, the same way you would.

So the real skill in RAG is the R: finding the right small piece. Most of the next lessons are about that.

New words today

RAG: look it up first, then answer using what you found.

Hallucination: a confident answer that is not true.

Prompt: the full message you send to the AI.

LLM: the kind of AI that writes text, like ChatGPT.

That is four. All of them, and every later one, are in the glossary.

If you remember one thing
RAG means: before the AI answers, find the right piece of your own documents and give it to the AI along with the question.

Next lesson: why the AI makes things up in the first place, which explains why this fix works.
exercise:
Try it by hand, five minutes. Open ChatGPT or any AI chat. Ask it something only your own documents know, like your company's leave policy or your team's on-call rule. Notice what it says. Then find the real paragraph, paste it above your question the way the example does, and ask again. You have just done RAG by hand.

Then reply to the email. One line is enough: "done", or the first word that confused you. The next lesson comes after you reply.
